facts.statement: Magnamanus was a herbivorous iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous in what is now Spain.
facts.quote: Magnamanus is an extinct genus of herbivorous iguanodontian dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Spain in the Golmayo Formation.

facts.statement: Magnamanus soriaensis lived approximately 130 million years ago during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous in Europe.
facts.quote: Magnamanus soriaensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Magnamanus de dinosaurio ornitisquioiguanodontiano que vivió a principios de período Cretácico hace aproximadamente 130 millones de años, durante el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Magnamanus was a large ornithopod measuring 9 to 10 meters long and weighing around 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: Magnamanus is a large ornithopod measuring 9 - 10 m long and weighing around 3 MT—a similar size to Iguanodon bernissartensis.

facts.statement: The species Magnamanus soriaensis was named and described in 2016 by Carolina Fuentes Vidarte, Manuel Calvo Meijide, Federico Meijide Fuentes, and Manuel Fuentes Meijide.
facts.quote: In 2016 the type species Magnamanus soriaensis was named and described by Carolina Fuentes Vidarte, Manuel Calvo Meijide, Federico Meijide Fuentes and Manuel Fuentes Meijide.

facts.statement: The genus name Magnamanus combines the Latin words for "large" and "hand" to reference the animal's big hands.
facts.quote: The genus name is a combination of the Latin word magnus "large" and manus, "hand", a reference to the big hands of the animal.

facts.statement: Fossils of Magnamanus were found in the Golmayo Formation, which dates to the Hauterivian-Barremian period, about 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossils, with catalogue numbers MNS 2000/132, 2001/122, 2002/95, 2003/69, 2004/54, were found in the Golmayo Formation which dates from the Hauterivian - Barremian, about 130 million years old.

facts.statement: Magnamanus is classified within the group Ankylopollexia in Styracosterna, occupying a rather basal position.
facts.quote: Magnamanus is classified within the group Ankylopollexia in Styracosterna, placed in a rather basal position.

facts.statement: Magnamanus is classified within the group Ankylopollexia, which is itself part of Styracosterna, in a relatively basal position.
facts.quote: Magnamanus es clasificado dentro del grupo Ankylopollexia que se encuentra a su vez dentro de Styracosterna, situado en una posición relativamente basal.

facts.statement: The width of the wrist in Magnamanus is 70% of the length of the hand.
facts.quote: The width of the wrist is 70% of the length of the hand.

facts.statement: The skeleton of Magnamanus, found between 2000 and 2004, is one of the most complete dinosaur skeletons from the Lower Cretaceous of Spain.
facts.quote: Between 2000 and 2004 they dug up the skeleton of a euornithopod, one of the most complete skeletons of a dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of Spain that has been found.

facts.statement: The genus Magnamanus was described by Fuentes Vidarte and colleagues in 2016.
Magnamanus belongs to the suborder Styracosterna.
Magnamanus is classified within the bird-hipped dinosaurs, Ornithischia.
Magnamanus lived during the Hauterivian to Barremian stages, between 132.6 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Magnamanus has been recorded so far.
